g1.label: 1. Sorry, I can’t play football on Sunday. I ___ my grandparents in Leipzig; we booked the train in October.
g1.why: A fixed personal arrangement, already booked, takes the present continuous.

g2.label: 2. – The printer is broken again. – Don’t worry, I ___ IT services and ask them to come.
g2.why: Will is for a decision made at the moment of speaking, like an offer.

g3.label: 3. Look at those dark clouds. It ___ rain before the barbecue starts.
g3.why: Going to is for a prediction based on what you can see now.

g4.label: 4. Can we ___ the dentist appointment? I have an exam that morning.
g4.why: Reschedule means change the date or time of an appointment.

g5.label: 5. The concert has been ___ until March because the singer is ill.
g5.why: Postponed means moved to a later date; until March shows the new time.

g6.label: 6. This time next week I ___ on a beach in Portugal, far away from my desk.
g6.why: The future continuous describes an action in progress at a future time.

g7.label: 7. By the end of my degree I ___ in three different countries.
g7.why: By the end of + a period takes the future perfect for a finished result.

g8.label: 8. Could you send me your ___ for next week? I’d like to find a time for a call.
g8.why: After your you need a noun: availability, the times when you are free.

g9.label: 9. After the job interview, send a short ___ email to thank them for their time.
g9.why: A follow-up email continues what happened at a meeting or interview.

g10.label: 10. Before the meeting, please read the ___: there are four points to discuss.
g10.why: The agenda lists the points to discuss; minutes record them afterwards.

g11.label: 11. We are ahead ___ schedule: the first two chapters of the thesis are already finished.
g11.why: Ahead of schedule means earlier than planned.

g12.label: 12. When I finally arrived at the study group, the others ___ already left.
g12.why: Already left before I arrived: the earlier past action takes the past perfect.
